notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 05/07/2025
Patient: Grover Stamm, 75-year-old male

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 05/07/2025. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 23.9 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 10% of all events. The remainder of respiratory events were obstructive in nature. Oxygen saturation showed intermittent drops associated with apneic episodes. Sleep architecture was disrupted with frequent arousals and decreased REM sleep. These findings indicate moderate sleep apnea with a mixed pattern of respiratory events. Treatment options will be reviewed with the patient.

Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 08/09/2026
Patient: Grover Stamm, 76-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Mr. Stamm has been using CPAP therapy for sleep apnea. He reports difficulty tolerating the device.

CPAP Data Review:
CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 2.5 hours per night on 39% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates poor adherence to CPAP therapy despite efforts to optimize mask fit. Given the documented intolerance, alternative treatment strategies should be considered.

Plan:
1. Discuss alternative therapies for sleep apnea.
2. Consider referral for oral appliance evaluation.
3. Schedule follow-up to reassess symptoms and treatment efficacy.

Summary:
Mr. Stamm is a 76-year-old male with sleep apnea who is unable to tolerate CPAP therapy despite mask refitting and support. Further management will focus on alternative options to improve sleep quality and reduce apnea events.
